title: Vasaloppet Endurance Base Building - Aerobic Capacity

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Move slowly and deliberately, synchronizing breath with movement. Warm up the spine and prepare nervous system for sustained effort.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Control the rotation through your hips. Feel the glute activation on each side. This prepares hip mobility for sustained skiing movements.

items.name: Rowing Machine
items.cues: Easy, conversational pace. Focus on consistent rhythm and full body engagement. Keep strokes smooth and controlled at RPE 3-4.

items.name: Ski Erg
items.cues: Maintain steady RPE 5-6 effort (can sustain conversation with difficulty). Keep a consistent rhythm using full body - drive through legs while engaging core. Focus on smooth, powerful strokes that mimic Vasaloppet poling mechanics. Monitor for any form breakdown as fatigue sets in.

items.name: Air Bike
items.cues: Easy spinning pace, RPE 4-5. Use this as active recovery while building aerobic capacity. Maintain steady cadence. Engage both legs and upper body with light arm involvement on the handle bars.

items.name: Cat-Cow
items.cues: Slow, controlled movements. Allow heart rate to gradually decrease while mobilizing the spine.

items.name: 90/90 Hip Switches
items.cues: Gentle rotation through hips. Focus on breathing and stretching the glutes and hip flexors.

items.name: Calf Stretch
items.cues: Hold each leg's calf stretch for 1 minute. Lean forward gently with one leg extended. Target the muscles heavily used in skiing and poling.

items.name: Biceps Wall Stretch
items.cues: Hold each arm's stretch for 1 minute against the wall. Gently rotate your body away to feel the shoulder and bicep stretch. Recovery focus for upper body.

rationale: Vasaloppet 90km race preparation requires building extensive aerobic base at RPE 5-6, the ideal zone for long-distance endurance adaptation. This workout uses ski erg as primary stimulus to develop sport-specific power and poling mechanics.

Following yesterday's 55-minute endurance session, today's 50-minute workout maintains training momentum while allowing for slight recovery variation. The ski erg/air bike combination develops both anaerobic threshold and true aerobic capacity needed for the 90km distance.

With 53 days until the event, this base-building phase prioritizes sustained, steady-state efforts over intensity. The progression from ski erg (race-specific) to air bike (active recovery) allows muscular adaptation while managing cumulative fatigue.
